newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas barely changed, trade thin, Q4 off.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas barely changed, trade thin, Q4 off.

text.p: UK spot natural gas prices were slightly softer in the fourth quarter on Friday but were mostly unchanged in thin trade in other periods, traders and brokers said.
Q4 was traded at 12.85 pence a therm, and by the close was bid at 12.80 pence. This compares with trade at 12.90 pence or possibly higher on Thursday.
But Q1 was assessed unchanged with no trade reported, and Q2 was only slightly softer on the offer and unchanged on the bid, following trade at 11.30 pence and 11.35 pence a therm.
There was also some trade done for the calendar year, at 12.90 pence and 12.925 pence a therm, but in most periods there was little activity and little serious interest.
"It's been desperately dull," said one trader,
One seller reported receiving interest for a Dec/Jan/Feb strip at St Fergus. The seller offered 15.80 pence a therm but reported no real interest at this month.

Requests for this strip have been quite common, he said, as many buyers are keen to avoid the whole of Q1 as they do not want large volumes of gas in March, a shoulder month between winter and spring.
"March and October appear to be the unwashed and unloved months," he said.
A trader said the flexibility mechanism had sold around 2.8 million therms at a System Marginal Price of 0.2954 pence a kiloWatt (around 8.66 pence a therm) hour on Friday.

An industry function on Thursday evening had gone on extremely late and helped contribute to the slow start to the day and the thin level of activity on Friday, dealers said. More than one reported late starts and sore heads, and a desire to do no more trade than was strictly necessary.

The IPE traded only 20 lots in a single deal. August traded at 9.325 pence a therm and settled at the same price, up by 0.025 pence from the previous day. Settlement prices were mixed, with some up and some down, but most of the movements were small.
